content:
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after bullish sentiment events or high supply net events; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such contexts.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; apply a 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature mean reversion.
- When sentiment is predominantly bullish (≥0.67) and supply net is negative, model underreacts; increase forecast baseline by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model overreacts; reduce forecast baseline by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to new events; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days for new auction supply events.
- For 30-day horizon, model shows persistent underestimation of true mean; apply a 2–4% upward bias to align with observed mean reversion toward higher prices.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to forecast flat; introduce a 1–2% upward trend to capture hidden bullish momentum.
